title: Medium throughput protocol for genome-based quantification of intracellular mycobacterial loads and macrophage survival during in vitro infection
protocol: Euthanize the mice using an approved procedure.
Remove tibia and femurs from euthanized mice, keeping some muscle tissue attached if necessary.
Store the removed bones in a 50 mL conical tube containing 10 mL Media 0 on ice.
Transfer the removed bones of each mouse into 10 mL ice-cold Media 0.
Gently crush the bones with a pestle in a mortar.
Remove the media to a clean tube placed on ice.
Add 10 mL of fresh ice-cold Media 0 to the mortar and repeat bone crushing.
Combine cell suspensions and store on ice.
Pour bone marrow fluid over a cell strainer placed on top of a clean 50 mL conical tube.
Dilute greasy tissues by adding Media 0 up to 50 mL in the conical tube.
Spin cells at 200 × g for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Resuspend cell pellets in 5 mL of Media 0 per each mouse.
Gently break clumps by pipetting up and down several times using wide-bore tips.
Add 5 mL of LymphoprepTM to a clean 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Carefully overlay the bone marrow suspension on top of the Lymphoprep layer.
Perform gradient centrifugation at 600 × g for 20 minutes at 20°C–25°C with brakes off.
Gently remove cells from the interface using a 5 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the collected cells into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add Media 0 to reach a total volume of 50 mL and centrifuge at 200 × g (1,000 rpm) for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cells in 10 mL Media 0, then centrifuge again at 200 × g (1,000 rpm) for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Resuspend cells in 5 mL Media 1, count them, and dilute to a final concentration of 1–3×10^6 cells/mL.
Add the diluted cells to a 25 cm² polystyrene tissue culture-treated flask.
Incubate for 24 hours at 37°C with 5% CO₂ in a humidified incubator.
Transfer all non-adherent cells from the 25 cm² flask to a new 75 cm² polystyrene tissue culture-treated flask.
Wash the 25 cm² flask with 10 mL Media 1 and transfer any remaining cells to the 75 cm² flask.
Incubate for two days at 37°C with 5% CO₂ in a humidified incubator.
Collect non-adherent cells on day 4, centrifuge at 200 × g (1,000 rpm) for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C, and resuspend them in 10 mL Media 3.
Count the collected cells and expect approximately 3–5 × 10^6 cells per mouse.
Dilute the cells to a final concentration of 2.5×10^5 cells/mL in Media 3.
Plate 1.5×106 cells per well in a 6 well ultra-low attachment plate.
Incubate cells for 2 days in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Collect all cells enriched after the initial incubation by pipetting up and down several times to avoid bubbles.
Centrifuge collected cells at 200 × g for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Resuspend cells in antibiotic-free media (Media 2).
Count and dilute the cells as needed.
Plate 15×103 cells per well in a 96 well plate using 200 μL volume of Media 2.
Incubate the plated cells for 2 days in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Replace 90% of old media with fresh pre-warmed (at 37°C) Media 2.
Incubate cells for an additional 2 days in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Prepare macrophage monolayers in antibiotic-free medium for at least 4 days prior to infection.
Include two media changes during preparation.
Replace the medium 1 day before infection.
Cells can be treated with cytokines or small molecules the day before infection.
Dilute 0.5–1.0 mL of a frozen Mtb stock in 5 mL of liquid culture medium (Middlebrook 7H9 Broth with OADC).
Add the diluted Mtb to a 30 mL square sterile media bottle and close tightly.
Place the bottle(s) and adsorbent paper in a secondary container with a leakage-proof lid.
Incubate at 37°C for 2–3 days in a shaking incubator at 100 rpm until OD600 = 0.4–0.5.
Avoid overgrowth to prevent clumping of bacteria.
Transfer the Mtb suspension from the media bottle to a sterile 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 2,100 × g (∼3,000 rpm) at 20°C–25°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of Media 2 pre-warmed to 37°C (avoid bubbles or foam).
Sonicate twice for 5 s each using a sonicating water-bath with a 5–10 s interval at 20°C–25°C.
Add 5 mL of pre-warmed Media 2, mix and leave the tube in a vertical position for 30–60 min at 20°C–25°C to let the residual clumps settle down.
Use the upper 8 mL for subsequent steps without disturbing the clumps at the bottom.
Remove plunger from a 10mL “control syringe” (BD, Cat. #309695).
Attach the syringe barrel to a 5 μm filter (Micron Separation) and place the filter on top of a 15 mL conical tube secured in a rack.
Transfer the top 8 mL of the Mtb suspension, insert the plunger and press to filter the bacterial suspension.
Hold the syringe, filter, and the reception tube with one hand and rapidly insert the plunger and gently press with the other hand.
Measure OD of the liquid Mtb bacterial culture at A600 using the dilution medium as a blank control.
Calculate the bacterial concentration assuming that after filtration single-cell Mtb suspension at OD600 = 1 is approx. 3×108 bacteria per mL.
Dilute the Mtb suspension with Media 2 to achieve the required concentration for macrophage infection.
Prepare 0.5 × 10^6 bacteria per mL in Media 2 for an MOI of 1:1, adding 0.1 mL per well in a 96-well format.
Dilute Mtb suspension by a factor of 60 when OD600 = 0.1 to achieve the desired concentration.
Plate an aliquot of Mtb on solid media and count colonies after 3 weeks to determine the precise infectious dose retrospectively.
Prepare avirulent vaccine strain of M. bovis BCG in the BSL2 lab using the same procedure as for Mtb.
Dilute BCG 10-fold in PBS after filtration, achieving a concentration of approximately 3–5 × 10^6 cells per mL to avoid clumping.
Store diluted BCG at 4°C up to 21 days.
Transfer 96-well plates containing macrophage cultures into the BSL3 facility.
Remove 50% volume (100 μL for a 96-well plate) of media prior to infection from each well.
Prepare bacterial suspensions for each MOI by diluting Mtb suspensions in Media 2.
Place 10 mL of diluted Mtb in a 100 mm petri dish.
Add 100 μL of the bacterial suspension to each well using a multichannel pipette.
Use centrifuge platforms with biocontainment lids for bacterial suspensions.
Centrifuge the plates at 200 × g for 5 min at 22°C–25°C.
Incubate the plates at 37°C, 5% CO2 and 95% humidity for 2 h.
Add amikacin (to a final concentration of 200 μg/mL) to eliminate extracellular bacteria.
Incubate with amikacin at 37°C, 5% CO2 and 95% humidity for 30–45 min.
Wash the cells 3 times with Media 4 at 20°C–25°C.
Replace 90% of the media in each well after washing to avoid drying of monolayers.
Incubate cells in a final volume of 200 μL Media 2 per well.
If needed, dilute the compound at 2× concentration in Media 2 and add 100 μL to each well containing macrophage monolayers in 100 μL of media.
Place plates inside secondary containers with covers slightly opened for gas exchange.
Incubate plates at 37°C, 5% CO2 and 95% humidity, changing medium every two days.
Carefully remove 90% of supernatant (180 μL for 96 well plate) from the infected plate and dispose into liquid waste container containing an undiluted approved disinfectant.
Carefully remove media from infected plates and dispose into liquid waste containers.
Wash cells once with washing media.
Add 100 μL of staining solution.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 and 95% humidity for 30 min in the dark.
Remove 90% (90 μL) staining solution and wash the cells 2 times with 200 μL washing media.
Carefully remove washing media and add 100 μL 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Incubate cells at 22°C–25°C for 30 min in dark.
Wash cells twice with washing media.
Cover the macrophage monolayer with washing media by adding a final volume of 200 μL per well.
Seal the plate with parafilm.
Wipe the sealed plate with an approved disinfectant.
Place the disinfected plate in a sealed container.
Safely remove the container from BSL3 following standard operating procedures.
Remove 90% of washing media from the infected plate (approximately 180 μL).
Add 100 μL/well Hoechst 33342 nuclear dye (final concentration 50 μg/mL) suspended in 1× PBS.
Incubate the plate at 20°C–25°C for 15 min in the dark.
Remove the Hoechst dye from the plate.
Add 200 μL/well of 1× PBS to the plate.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil.

Image and analyze the total and dead cell numbers using the Nexcelom Celigo imaging cytometer (select Live-or-Dye™ 594/614 Fixable Viability dye fluorescence for dead cells and Hoechst stain for total cells).
Resuspend stock solution of Sera-Mag SpeedBeads by vortexing.
Vortex magnetic beads until the solution becomes uniformly distributed (vortex 4–5 times for 5 s each).
Aliquot 3 mL beads into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 20 mL of 1× TE buffer and pellet beads in a magnetic rack for 20-30 min at 20°C-25°C.
Remove 1× TE buffer without disturbing magnetic beads and repeat the addition and removal steps once more.
Resuspend the beads in 5 mL of nuclease-free water.
Add resuspended beads to PEG buffer (approximately 140 mL).
Wash the 50 mL conical tube with another 5 mL of nuclease-free water and add it to the PEG buffer.
Store the PEG buffer containing magnetic beads at 4°C in the dark.
Remove 1× PBS from the plate and add 200 μL/well of a 30 mM glycine solution in 1× PBS for 5 minutes to quench PFA.
Remove the glycine solution and wash cells twice with 1× PBS.
Aliquot sufficient volume of lysis buffer containing Proteinase K (50 μL per well).
Add BCG to the lysis buffer and mix.
Remove 1× PBS from each well.
Add 50 μL of the lysis buffer stock solution containing BCG to each well.
Incubate the plate at 60°C for 45 min to lyse macrophages and release bacteria.
Transfer the lysate to a PCR plate.
Heat the PCR plate at 95°C for 45 min to lyse bacteria (Mtb and BCG).
Centrifuge the plate for 1 min at 200 × g to collect liquid at the bottom.
Add an equal volume (50 μL) of neutralization buffer to the lysate.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down.
Incubate the PCR plate at 22°C–25°C for 15–20 min after adding SPRI magnetic bead suspension.
Place the PCR plate on a magnetic plate and allow precipitation of magnetic beads for 15–20 min.
Carefully remove flow-through without disturbing or removing any magnetic beads.
Add 180 μL of 70% ethanol per well to wash the SPRI magnetic beads.
Incubate the plate for 2 min at 22°C–25°C and remove 70% ethanol keeping the PCR plate on the magnetic plate.
Repeat the wash step two more times, removing ethanol each time.
Remove PCR plate from the magnetic plate and incubate at 37°C for 15 min to evaporate residual ethanol.
Add 40 μL nuclease-free water, mix by pipetting up and down.
Incubate at 22°C–25°C for 15–20 min to elute DNA from the beads.
Place the PCR plate back on the magnetic plate at 22°C–25°C for 2 min.
Keeping the PCR plate on the magnetic plate, carefully transfer 35 μL of isolated and enriched DNA to a new PCR plate.
Cap the plate and store it at −20°C for long-term storage or continue to the qPCR step.
Thaw TaqMan Environmental Master Mix 2.0 on ice, protected from light.
Thaw Mtb and BCG primers/probes on ice, protected from light.
Mix the master mix by pipetting up and down.
Invert Mtb and BCG primers and probes 3–4 times.
Briefly spin to collect liquid at the bottom of tubes.
Determine the number of reactions based on the number of wells in a 96-well plate.
Mix by gently pipetting up and down.
Centrifuge briefly at 4°C for 15 seconds at 1,000 × g.
Dispense 11 μL of the master mix reaction into a new 96 well PCR plate (Bio-Rad Cat. #MLL9601).
Add 9 μL template DNA isolated using magnetic beads protocol, step 52 c.
Seal the plate and centrifuge briefly at 4°C for 1 minute at 200 × g.
Turn on the qPCR machine and allow the block to equilibrate.
Set up a program with a total run time of approximately 120 minutes.
Load the 96-well plate and start the run.
Quantify standard quantity (SQ) of DNA in 9 μL template using standard concentration of BCG or Mtb DNA.
Multiply the SQ by the amount of DNAse-free water used for DNA elution from magnetic beads.
Calculate the SQ in femtograms.
Multiply the values from step 56 c (in femtograms) by 2.06 to quantify total genome equivalents per well.
Subtract the Mtb Ct values from BCG Ct values for corresponding wells: [Ct Mtb - Ct BCG = x].
Calculate the fold change as compared to the BCG standard using 2-x.
Normalize the Mtb load per well adjusting for the total cell number in that well.
Use the total number of macrophages (live and dead) per well to normalize the Mtb load to account for cell loss during Mtb infection.
Calculate the average Mtb load for the untreated Mtb-infected control (UTC) group.
Divide the values in each well by the UTC average to determine fold Mtb change per well.
Perform appropriate statistical analysis (unpaired t-test, for example).
